findings.title: Hung spawn-context flushers are never killed on Linux
findings.body: Restart and shutdown treat flusher children as multiprocessing.Process before calling kill() or terminate(). Production processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which yields SpawnProcess. On Linux that class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the fork context class bound when multiprocessing is imported), so both isinstance checks are false. A hung flusher is therefore left running, and _create_process_for_shards immediately starts another process on the same shards. Both call flush_segments, produce to buffered-segments, and done_flush_segments, so segments are duplicated and Redis flush state races. healthy_since is reset on restart and then updated by the new process, so the hang detector will not notice the leftover process. The same check at join() (line 346) also skips terminate(), so a flusher blocked in Kafka future.result() is not stopped on shutdown. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, or exclude threading.Thread, instead of multiprocessing.Process.

findings.title: Replacement flusher starts before the old process exits
findings.body: After the restart path tries to kill a flusher, it never join()s that process or waits until is_alive() is false before _create_process_for_shards starts a new one for the same shard list. kill() only sends SIGKILL and returns. Until the old process is actually dead it can still be inside flush_segments or producing a batch it already read, while the new process reads those same shards and produces again. done_flush_segments then runs in both processes. That duplicates segments on the buffered-segments topic and races Redis cleanup. The old Process object is also dropped without join(), so repeated restarts leave unreaped children.

findings.title: Join timeout abandons still-running flusher processes
findings.body: join() gives next_step.join the full timeout, then walks flusher processes against the same deadline. As soon as remaining time is <= 0 it breaks out of the loop and never terminate()s the current or later processes. With more than one flusher, the first process can consume the whole remaining timeout in the is_alive() wait, and every other process is left running. Those children are daemon processes, so they keep flushing and producing until the parent eventually exits, which can kill them mid-produce before done_flush_segments. Shutdown should terminate every still-alive process after the deadline instead of breaking, and join() each of them so they are reaped.

findings.title: Flusher metric shard tags are comma-joined and inconsistent
findings.body: shard_tag is every shard id for that process joined with commas, and it is sent as a single tag value. The consumer flag defaults to one flusher process, so in production this value is the full assigned-shard list (for example "0,1,2,...,31"). DogStatsD encodes tags as comma-separated key:value pairs, so a comma inside the value splits the metric into garbage tags and drops or mis-attributes spans.buffer.flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes. The tag also changes with every partition assignment, so it cannot be aggregated per shard. wait_produce makes this worse by using the different key "shards" (line 199) while produce uses "shard" (line 185), so the two timers cannot be correlated. Emit one tag value per shard, or omit the tag when a process handles more than one shard, and use the same key on both timers.

findings.title: Consumer test sleep cannot actually wait for the flusher
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at line 15, then calls time.sleep(0.1) specifically to let the flusher thread observe the drift update before join(). That call is the patched no-op, so it does not yield or wait. join() sets stopped immediately; if the flusher has not yet flushed with the new drift, it exits and the assertion that one segment was produced fails intermittently. The production spawn/kill/join path is also untested: produce_to_pipe forces threads, so the SpawnProcess isinstance bug and multi-process flush behavior never run in CI. Wait with a real sleep saved before the patch, and cover at least one multi-shard flush plus process restart.
